answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it can trade, sized to the value it moves. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, and misbehavior burns the bond instead of just the identity. Reputation accrues slowly, like yarrow spreading roots, so a fresh identity starts as an ember of trust and must earn its way toward the zenith through verified, paid work. Attackers risk real capital per identity, while honest agents recover their bond by behaving well.
